title: The only dist-staleness detector (session-start-init-check) is advisory-only, fires at NEXT SessionStart, checks the wrong target (repo dist DIR-mtime, never active ~/.claude dist), and uses a coarse dir-mtime comparison that an in-place cp can defeat on Windows
observe_how: Read the freshness block: it gates on `projectDir.includes('continuous-claude')` and stats `.claude/hooks/dist` (the REPO dir), comparing each src .ts mtime to the dist DIRECTORY mtime. It never inspects ~/.claude/hooks/dist (what actually runs). It only pushes a `maintenanceWarnings` string; it never blocks and never rebuilds. So a stale dist that ran the entire session surfaces only as text at the next session start, in the repo project only.
telemetry: Compare per-file: for each src X.ts, stat the corresponding dist X.mjs (not the dir); and run the check against ACTIVE ~/.claude/hooks/dist, not the repo. Better: a SessionStart that rebuilds-or-blocks rather than printing a warning the model may ignore.

title: architecture-stats-sync fires a DETACHED background `sync-architecture-stats.mjs --apply` on every watched commit, rewriting tracked architecture.json AFTER the commit -> perpetual post-commit working-tree dirt (the `M architecture.json` in this session's git status)
observe_how: Hook is PostToolUse:Bash; on a commit touching .claude/{hooks,agents,skills}/ or scripts/ it spawns detached `node scripts/sync-architecture-stats.mjs --apply` which writes docs/architecture/system-visualization/architecture.json. Because it runs AFTER the commit, the regenerated file is left uncommitted. The review's own session `git status` opened with `M docs/architecture/system-visualization/architecture.json`; architecture-stats-sync.log confirms it fired ('done: stats synced.').
telemetry: Count how often `git status` is non-clean solely due to architecture.json after a commit. Either (a) make the sync part of pre-commit so it lands in the same commit, or (b) gitignore the generated artifact and regenerate on demand.

evidence.quote:

title: Facade bus discovery skips Q7's persisted-file recovery: approximates the bus id from raw COORDINATION_SESSION_ID, then falls back to most-recent-mtime context.json — under concurrent sessions it silently biases recall from ANOTHER session's bus

evidence.quote: Persisted to file on first call so subprocesses can recover.

* BOUNDARY (finding #15): this is a SECOND exported function, NOT a merge.
 * Coordination callers (session-register.ts / file-claims.ts) keep their
 * existing COORDINATION_SESSION_ID-first chain in shared/session-id.ts

observe_how: Read discoverBus() in scripts/code-intel.mjs:119-160. getSessionId() persists the session signal to ~/.claude/.coordination-session-id (session-id.ts chain), which the facade could read to reconstruct the exact bus id; instead it uses the env var (often unset in a bare shell) and then mtime. With two terminals on the same project, the facade reads whichever session wrote last (warning only, bias still applied). Also new instance for SEED-12: this is now a THIRD bus/session-id derivation alongside session-id.ts and session-isolation.ts.
causal_links: SEED-12 (two competing getSessionId schemes; the facade adds an approximation of a third)
